question: How many licensed traffic engineers must a road agency employ per 100 centerline miles to comply with the MUTCD?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence contains no provision requiring a road agency to employ any specific number of licensed traffic engineers per centerline mile, and no such ratio appears anywhere in the material provided. The MUTCD's compliance requirements concern the traffic control devices themselves, not agency staffing levels, and the Manual explicitly does not even mandate that an engineer make the final implementation decision. The evidence is therefore insufficient to support any staffing ratio. Standards (mandatory): - "The Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices for Streets and Highways (MUTCD) is incorporated by reference in 23 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Part 655, Subpart F and shall be recognized as the national standard for all traffic control devices installed on any street, highway, bikeway, or site roadway open to public travel..." — this establishes a standard for devices, not for agency staffing. - "In cases involving Federal-aid projects... the traffic control devices installed (temporary or permanent) shall comply with the most recent edition of the National MUTCD before that highway is opened or re-opened to the public for unrestricted travel" — again, compliance attaches to the devices, not to a number of engineers employed. Citations: - Section 1B.01 Standard §1 (p.4) - Section 1B.03 Standard §4 (p.5) - Section 1D.03 Support §4 (p.32) - Section 1A.04 Support §1 (p.2)
